claims.statement: The integration_settings table is keyed by a stable string `key` and stores `encrypted_value` plus `is_secret`, `updated_by`, and timestamps; per-Page Facebook tokens are dynamic rows keyed by `facebook_page_token:<page_id>`.

IntegrationSettingsCipher wraps every secret in AES-GCM with a 12-byte random nonce and stores the result as `v1:<base64(nonce||ciphertext)>`; the key is `SHA-256(INTEGRATION_SETTINGS_ENCRYPTION_KEY)`, falling back to `SHA-256(JWT_SECRET)` only in `app_env == development`.

Settings.model_post_init refuses to boot when `app_env != "development"` and either `jwt_secret` remains the committed dev default or `integration_settings_encryption_key` is empty, so a production instance cannot sign admin JWTs with a public key or skip encryption.

Per-Page Facebook tokens are stored as `v2:` rows whose AEAD associated data is the Page id, so a ciphertext produced for Page A fails to decrypt under Page B (`InvalidTag`); `decrypt_with_context` falls back to the legacy `v1:` path only for unconverted rows.
IntegrationSettingsService.admin_view() returns only `{configured, preview: '<first4>...<last4>'}` for each secret, with short values fully masked; the admin API is gated by `require_admin`.

Every chatbot turn asks IntegrationSettingsService for a frozen runtime config (ZaloRuntimeConfig, MinimaxRuntimeConfig, OpenRouterRuntimeConfig, FacebookRuntimeConfig); the service is built inside graph.factories.build_deps and resolves DB rows with env-var fallback.

Secret-bearing caches live in `_LOCAL_SECRET_CACHE` keyed by namespace + version + key_prefix and never enter Redis; the LLM-client cache is keyed only by the `integration_minimax` and `integration_openrouter` versions, so a Zalo rotation never tears down the cached LLM clients.

ZaloChannelSender receives a `refresh=lambda: integration_settings.refresh_oa_access_token()` closure; refresh is guarded by a Redis `SET NX EX` lock so RQ workers do not refresh in parallel, and losers re-read the token the winner just stored.

Admin updates encrypt the value, upsert the IntegrationSetting row, record an audit row tagged `update_zalo_integration_settings` listing changed keys (never values), commit, evict the local cache namespace, and bump the namespace version so subsequent reads decrypt fresh.

Decrypt failures (`InvalidTag`) are caught, logged with the key name only, and the row is skipped so callers fall back to env vars instead of 500ing the admin view; key rotation therefore requires a maintenance window that re-writes affected rows.
